name: MonarchLoadingState
title: LoadingState
summary: A placeholder for a region that is loading: skeleton rows, cards or a detail layout, or a progress ring with a label, announced once.
whenToUse: While the first page of a list, a set of cards or a detail screen loads and its layout is known.
whenNotToUse: For a short wait inside a button, use the loading state of MonarchButton. For a known amount of work, use MonarchProgress with a value. For one placeholder shape, use MonarchSkeleton.
api: @Composable fun MonarchLoadingState(label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchLoadingStateVariant = MonarchLoadingStateVariant.List, rows: Int = 4)
enum class MonarchLoadingStateVariant { List, Rows, Cards, Detail, Spinner }

options.name: label
options.description: What is loading, such as "Loading tickets". Announced; shown by the spinner variant.

options.name: variant
options.description: List (avatar and two lines), Rows (a line and a short value), Cards (blocks), Detail (a title and paragraphs) or Spinner.

options.name: rows
options.description: The rows or cards drawn by List, Rows and Cards. Negative counts draw none.

states.name: skeleton
states.description: MonarchSkeleton placeholders in the chosen layout; the shimmer stands still when animations are off.

states.name: spinner
states.description: An indeterminate progress ring with the label under it.

appearance: Skeletons use the muted background with a subtle shimmer. The ring takes the accent solid color on the emphasis track; the label is muted label text. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web marks the region aria-busy; Compose has no busy state, so the label is announced once through a polite live region filled after the first frame, as iOS posts an announcement. The web Cards layout is a grid; here cards are stacked, because the placeholder takes the width it is given. iOS shares the name and the variants.
accessibility: The skeletons and the ring are hidden from TalkBack.
The label is set on a polite live region after the first frame, so TalkBack announces it once; it can also be reached by swiping.
In the spinner variant the visible label is that live region, so it is read once, not twice.
The spinner label wraps at the largest font size.
edgeCases: rows = 0 or below draws no rows, but the label is still announced.
Replacing the loading state with the content does not announce the content; say what loaded, for example with the count, when it matters.
